steps.body: To compare two lengths fairly, start them from the same line. Then whichever reaches farther is longer.
steps.narration: To compare two lengths fairly, start them from the same line. Then whichever reaches farther is longer.

widget.prompt: Make the compare fair, then tap the longer ribbon.
widget.unalignedFeedback: Looks can trick you — line the starting ends up first.
widget.missFeedback: Now the starts are lined up — check the far ends again: the one reaching farther is longer.
widget.successFeedback: Same start makes the compare fair — the bottom ribbon really does reach farther.

predict.prompt: One ribbon starts further along than the other. Can you trust the far ends alone?
predict.reveal: A shifted start can make the shorter ribbon reach farther, so aligning comes first.

misconceptions: Reading a length from appearance or position instead of from same-size units laid end to end.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same measurement?

explanationVariants: A fair compare needs a common start.

widget.prompt: Two ribbons lie side by side but one starts 3 units further along. What must you do before deciding which is longer? Choose the key measurement idea.

options.label: Compare the far ends as they lie
options.feedback: With one object shifted 3 units forward, the far ends alone can make the shorter one look longer.

options.label: Line up one end of both first
options.feedback: Correct — a fair comparison starts both objects from the same place, then the far ends decide.

options.label: Pick whichever looks bigger
options.feedback: Appearance is exactly what a shifted starting point distorts; align first, then judge.

options.label: Count the gap between them
options.feedback: The space between two objects describes their positions, not either object's length.

widget.prompt: Slide the red strip to the start line, then tap the longer strip.
widget.unalignedFeedback: The red strip starts ahead, so line up both starting ends before comparing.
widget.missFeedback: Now both strips begin together. Check which far end reaches farther.
widget.successFeedback: Both starts match, and the red strip reaches farther than the blue string.

widget.prompt: The ribbon is 10 cubes long and the pencil is 7 cubes long. How many cubes longer is the ribbon? Show the comparison result.

commonErrors.feedback: That is the whole length of the ribbon, not the extra it has beyond the pencil.
That is the length of the pencil, not the difference between the two.
